reading.title: Climate Change and Coral Reefs
reading.passage: Coral reefs are among the most biodiverse ecosystems on Earth, supporting over 25% of all marine species despite covering less than 1% of the ocean floor. However, rising ocean temperatures and acidification threaten their survival. When water temperatures increase even by 1-2 degrees Celsius, corals expel their symbiotic algae in a process called bleaching, which can lead to death. Conservation efforts including marine protected areas and reducing carbon emissions are essential to preserve these vital ecosystems for future generations.

questions.q: According to the passage, what percentage of marine species do coral reefs support?
options: Over 10%
Over 25%
Over 50%
Over 75%
questions.explanation: 지문에 'supporting over 25% of all marine species'라고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What does the term 'bleaching' refer to in the passage?
options: The process of cleaning coral reefs
When corals expel their symbiotic algae
The formation of new coral colonies
The acidification of ocean water
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'corals expel their symbiotic algae in a process called bleaching'이라고 설명합니다.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a conservation effort?
options: Marine protected areas
Reducing carbon emissions
Installing artificial reefs
Temperature control
questions.explanation: 지문에서 언급된 보존 노력은 해양 보호 지역과 탄소 배출 감소뿐이며, 인공 산호초 설치는 언급되지 않았습니다.

listening.title: University Library Services
listening.script: Student: Excuse me, I'm new to the university and I'm not sure how to use the library resources. Librarian: Of course! Welcome to our library. We offer many services including access to online databases, research assistance, and study spaces. We have computers, quiet study areas, and group collaboration rooms. Student: That sounds great! Do I need any special registration? Librarian: You just need your student ID card. Also, we offer workshops every week on how to search databases effectively and cite sources properly. You can find the schedule on our website. Student: Perfect! One more question—what's the late fee for books? Librarian: Books are typically due in three weeks, and the late fee is one dollar per day. However, you can renew books online before the due date if you need them longer. Student: Thank you so much for the information! Librarian: You're welcome! Feel free to ask any of our staff if you need further assistance.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this conversation?
options: To explain library policies to a new student
To discuss late fees and book renewal policies
To register the student for library access
To schedule a workshop on database searching
questions.explanation: 사서가 새로운 학생에게 도서관의 다양한 서비스와 자원에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 주요 목적은 새로운 학생에게 도서관 정책을 설명하는 것입니다.

questions.q: According to the librarian, what services are available for students?
options: Only computer access and quiet study areas
Online databases, research assistance, study spaces, and workshops
Group study rooms and book lending only
Database access and book renewal services only
questions.explanation: 사서가 '온라인 데이터베이스 접근, 연구 지원, 스터디 공간, 그리고 정기적인 워크숍'을 제공한다고 언급했습니다.

questions.q: What is the late fee for returning books after the due date?
options: Five dollars per day
One dollar per week
One dollar per day
No late fee with online renewal
